originalNode.title: The Coordinate Plane
originalNode.goal: Plot and read points on a grid.

quiz.prompt: In which quadrant does the point (-3, 2) lie?
quiz.explain: A negative x with a positive y places the point in the upper-left region, Quadrant II.

quiz.prompt: Which of these points lies exactly on the x-axis?
quiz.explain: A point is on the x-axis when its y-coordinate is 0, as in (5, 0).

quiz.prompt: The points (2, 1), (6, 1) and (6, 4) are three corners of a rectangle whose sides run along the grid lines. What is the x-coordinate of the fourth corner?
quiz.explain: The fourth corner sits at (2, 4), directly above the corner at (2, 1), so its x-coordinate is 2.

quiz.prompt: A counter starts at (3, 5), moves 4 squares left and then 2 squares down. What is its new y-coordinate?
quiz.explain: Moving left changes x alone. Moving down 2 takes y from 5 to 3.

quiz.prompt: A rectangle has corners at (1, 1), (7, 1), (7, 5) and (1, 5). What is its area in square units?
quiz.explain: The rectangle is 6 units wide and 4 units tall, so its area is 6 x 4 = 24. The 20 is its perimeter.

quiz.prompt: Point A sits at (-4, -1). Which move puts it into Quadrant I?
quiz.answer: Add 6 to x and 3 to y
choices: Add 6 to x and leave y
Add 3 to y and leave x
Add 6 to x and 3 to y
quiz.explain: Quadrant I needs both coordinates positive. Adding 6 and 3 gives (2, 2); changing one coordinate alone leaves the other negative.

quiz.prompt: A counter at (2, -3) moves 7 squares up. What is its new y-coordinate?
quiz.explain: Moving up adds to the y-coordinate: -3 + 7 = 4. The x-coordinate is unchanged.

quiz.prompt: How many units apart are the points (1, 4) and (7, 4) along the grid?
quiz.explain: The y-coordinates match, so the points lie on a horizontal line and the gap is 7 - 1 = 6 units.

quiz.prompt: A student plots the point (3, 5) by first going up 3 and then across 5. Which point did they actually mark?
quiz.explain: Coordinates are written across first, then up: (3, 5) means 3 right and 5 up. Reversing the order lands you on (5, 3).

quiz.prompt: A point has a negative x-coordinate and a negative y-coordinate. Where on the grid does it sit?
quiz.explain: Left of the y-axis and below the x-axis is the bottom-left region, Quadrant III; the quadrants are numbered anticlockwise from the top right.

lesson_media.alt: A path moves left three and up two to plot negative three, two in Quadrant Two.
lesson_media.caption: Read x first, then y; points on an axis are not inside a quadrant.

lesson_media.title: Across first, then up or down
lesson_media.instructions: Change x and y. Follow the dashed path from the origin to P; keep the order of the coordinates.

originalBinding.instructions: Drag or use the camera buttons to inspect the object from different sides. Change the labeled controls, then compare the geometry with the explanation below.
originalBinding.context: The Coordinate Plane: Inspect an explicit coordinate example from several directions and distinguish an input coordinate from a plotted output height.
